title: Balance a powered-off camera gimbal on its free tilt axis
instruction: Balance the powered-off camera on its tilt axis. Secure the sliding plate, then let go at each green mark, about 30 degrees up and down, for three seconds each.
context: Camera operators rebalance a gimbal after changing its lens. A front-heavy camera falls when the motor is off. Move the camera on its rail while supporting it and leave the tilt bearing free.
setup: A bench-mounted single-axis tilt rig carries a 620 g camera and lens. The other axes and camera height are pre-adjusted. An orange spring-applied rail brake opens when squeezed toward its outer grip. A pointer and two green marks indicate the two test angles.
scoring: Move the rail at least 8 mm while the brake is open. With it closed and the hands clear, release within 2 degrees of either 30-degree mark at no more than 5 deg/s. For 3 s, remain within 3 degrees of the mark and release angle and within 0.5 mm of the rail setting. One direction earns 0.5 and both earn 1.0. Opening the brake again or moving the adjusted rail more than 0.5 mm invalidates the previous verification.
reset_notes: Fixed lens and layout. Start with the slide centered in its travel reference, leaving the payload front-heavy.
fidelity: Rigid compound camera, a free tilt bearing, constrained dovetail travel and spring-loaded friction shoe. Other gimbal axes are fixed. Mass distribution, friction and clamp spring are prototype values.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 after 2400 steps (120 simulated seconds); termination: step_limit. Scripted/teleoperated demo: 1 after 1203 steps.
